title: fix(app-shell,react): lookup links on record pages and custom pages carry the console base path (objectui#12233)
body:
Fixes #12233
Clause-②: no

Item 4 of the list card objectui#12211. The parent stays open for its other items.

## What was wrong

A console can be mounted under a router basename. Hosted HotCRM serves it at `/_console`. On a record page, a valued lookup renders as a real anchor through `ReferencedRecordLink` in `@object-ui/fields`, which takes its href from the host's `RelatedRecordActionsValue.recordHref`. On the record page that host is `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`, which `RecordDetailView` mounts around the whole page. Its builder returned the bare router path `/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID?from=…`.

- A plain left click worked. The anchor hands it to `openRecord`, which calls `navigate`, and `navigate` adds the basename.
- A new tab, a middle-click or a copied link sent the browser to the bare route on the server, which answers `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`.

## Premise check, on objectui `origin/main` `6eca5b5a7`

- The console's `BrowserRouter basename` comes from the injected base tag (`resolveBasename` in `apps/console/src/App.tsx`), so a hosted console's router lives at `/_console`. Confirmed.
- `ReferencedRecordLink` is the only anchor in `@object-ui/fields` that draws a record link. `LookupCellRenderer` uses it for every valued lookup. The owner link is a lookup to `sys_user` through the same renderer, and `UserCellRenderer` draws no link.
- Only the bridge's builder adds the `?from=` trail that the measured href carries, so the bridge is the producer.
- `RecordDetailView` has two other record-route literals: the favourite entry and the recent-item entry. Both are router paths, and their readers use `navigate` and router `Link`s, so they are correct as they are. This PR leaves `RecordDetailView.tsx` untouched.
- The list page's producer (`listRecordActionsValue` in `ObjectView.tsx`) already returns a document path, because it derives from `window.location.pathname`, which includes the basename. The two producers disagreed. Applying the basename in the consumers would have doubled it on the list page, so the fix belongs in the producer.

## The fix

Round 2 (head `cc0777aa`) extends round 1 to the second producer of the same defect, under surface amendment `6123360584` on objectui#12233. Both hosts that publish `RelatedRecordActionsValue.recordHref` now share one join. These are the record page's `RelatedRecordActionsBridge` and the custom page's `pageRecordActionsValue`. The join is `documentHref(rootHref, routerPath)`, in the internal module `packages/app-shell/src/views/documentHref.ts`:

- Each host keeps one router-path builder (`recordPath`). `openRecord` navigates by that router path, as before, and the router adds the basename.
- `recordHref` returns `documentHref(useHref('/'), path)`: the router's own root href, which carries the basename, joined to the path. It equals the href react-router's `Link` renders for that route. A console mounted at the root keeps the bare href.
- `PageView` reads `useHref('/')` beside its other router hooks and passes it to `pageRecordActionsValue`, which takes it as a new fourth argument.

No widget changes. No `/_console` or `BASE_URL` literal is added anywhere.

## Published contract

- `RelatedRecordActionsValue.recordHref` is a member of a published type in `@object-ui/react`. Its type is unchanged. Round 2 adds one sentence to its doc: the value is a document href and carries the host router's basename, while `openRecord` navigates by the router path. Both producers now meet that doc.
- `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`, `pageRecordActionsValue` and `documentHref` are not reachable from the `@object-ui/app-shell` entry. Its `exports` are `.` and `./styles.css`, and the barrels name none of the three; `PageView` in the same barrels is the positive control.
- No package entry gains or loses an export, a prop or a type member. The only signature change is on the internal `pageRecordActionsValue`. That is the basis for `Clause-②: no`.
- The changeset declares `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch` and `@object-ui/react` `patch` (doc only).

## Tests

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/RelatedRecordActionsBridge.basenameHref-12233.test.tsx` (round 1). It mounts the real bridge under a `MemoryRouter`, with the real `LookupCellRenderer` for the three measured links (account, contact, and owner on `sys_user`):
  - with basename `/_console`, each href equals react-router's `Link` href and keeps `?from=`;
  - a left click routes to the named record with the basename applied once;
  - a no-basename control keeps the bare route.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/PageView.lookupHrefBasename-12233.test.tsx` (round 2). It mounts the real `PageView` under a real `MemoryRouter`, with the real `LookupCellRenderer`. It checks basename `/_console` against a react-router `Link` oracle and the left-click destination, with a no-basename control.
- `PageView.recordNavigator-11293.test.tsx` gains a basename case, and its builder calls pass `'/'` explicitly; no assertion is weakened.
- Four `PageView` tests gain a `useHref` entry returning `'/'` in their `react-router-dom` factory mock: `PageView.test.tsx`, `PageView.context-9673`, `PageView.editInStudioNeedsAuthoring-10899` and `page-kind-writing-end-9718`. Without it they fail; see B2.

Reverse checks, each from a committed fix through `ablation-replace`. In each, the anchor hit once and the blob changed, and the restore was proven: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

- **A1** (at `3a5e7950`): the bridge's href goes back to the bare router path. Result: `Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3)`, `expected '/apps/hotcrm/crm_account/record/A-1' to be '/_console/apps/hotcrm/crm_account/record/A-1'`.
- **A2** (at `3a5e7950`): the naive fix, where a left click navigates with the prefixed href. Result: `Tests 1 failed | 2 passed (3)`, with a doubled basename.
- **B1** (at `cc0777aa`): `pageRecordActionsValue`'s href goes back to the bare path. Result: `Tests 2 failed | 6 passed (8)`, Expected `/_console/apps/crm/account/record/A-1`, Received `/apps/crm/account/record/A-1`; the controls stay green.
- **B2** (at `cc0777aa`): `useHref` dropped from `PageView.test.tsx`'s mock. Result: `Error: [vitest] No "useHref" export is defined on the "react-router-dom" mock`.

**Declared narrowing of the test run.** The run covers every `packages/app-shell` and `apps/console` test whose source names any of these: the bridge, `RecordDetailView`, `recordHref`, `openRecord`, `LookupCellRenderer`, `ReferencedRecordLink`, `AppContent`, `ConsoleShell`, `useRelatedRecordActions`, `RelatedRecordActionsProvider`, `PageView`, `pageRecordActions` or `documentHref`. It also covers such tests elsewhere that import `@object-ui/app-shell`, all 109 `@object-ui/react` test files, and `packages/fields/src/__tests__/lookupCellRecordLink.test.tsx`. The full `@object-ui/app-shell` suite is left to CI's `Test` shards, which are green on this head.

## Acceptance notes

- **Sibling PR coordination:** objectui#12198's branch adds a test that mounts `PageView` under a `react-router-dom` mock with no `useHref`. Whichever PR lands second needs a `useHref` entry returning `'/'` in that mock. The seat has handed this to objectui#12198's dev.
- **Other record routes:** `RecordDetailView`'s favourite and recent-item record routes are router paths read through `navigate` and router `Link`s, so they are correct as they are and untouched.
